chunks: Indeed it is God who splits up the seed and the kernel, and brings forth the living from the dead, the dead from the living. This is God: So whither do you stray?
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Faliq al-habb wa al-nawa' in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is often cited to demonstrate the continuity between physical creation and spiritual resurrection, highlighting Allah's absolute authority over both the material and immaterial realms. The phrase 'Faliq al-hab wa al-nawa' (He who splits the grain and the stone) underscores the precision of divine power, serving as a logical proof for the resurrection of the body. This concept reinforces the Shia belief in the tangible reality of the Hereafter, linking natural signs to theological truths.
